div.head: IV Eg 16
div.ab: Ic beo eow swyðe hold hlaford þa hwile þe me lif gelæst, ⁊ eow eallum swyðe bliðe eom, for þý þe ge swa georne ymbe frið syndon.
Ic beo eow swyðe hold hlaford þa hwyle þe me lif gelæst, ⁊ eow eallum swyðe bliðe eom, for ði þe ge swa georne ymbe frið syndon.

Quamdiu etenim comes fuerit uita, fidelis omnibus uobis perseuerabo. Et nunc omnes uos in uisceribus Christi commendo, ut magis ác magis abundetis in omni bonitate et scientia et opere bono. Ualete feliciter in Christo!
Ic beo eow swyðe hold hlaford þa hwyle þe me lif gelæst, ⁊ eow eallum swyðe bliðe eom, for ði þe ge swa georne ymbe frið syndon.
Ich bleibe euch ein sehr gnädiger Herr, so lange wie mir das Leben dauert, und bleibe euch allen recht gewogen, weil ihr so eifrig um die öffentliche Sicherheit [bemüht] seid.
I shall be a very gracious lord to you as long as my life lasts, and I am well disposed to you all, because you are so zealous for [public] peace.
I will be a very gracious lord to you as long as my life lasts. I am very well pleased with you all, because you are so zealous for the preservation of the public peace.

In C zeichnen den Schlusssatz rothverzierte Uncialen aus; es folgt der Angelsächs. Text, oben S. 206. U. f. in C. fehlt Hk.
In C the closing sentence is marked out by uncials decorated in red; there follows the Anglo-Saxon text, above p. 206. U. f. in C. Missing in Hk.
there follows in Latin Coena Domini.
S. o. 12⁷. Die Versio braucht das Lateinische fidelis in der Beziehung auch des Herrn zum Manne (für die ich es in den Wbb. nicht vermerkt finde), vielleicht nur weil hold gegenseitig gilt
See above 12⁷. The Versio uses the Latin fidelis also for the relation of the lord to his man (for which I do not find it recorded in the dictionaries), perhaps only because hold applies reciprocally
Hier redet Eadgar wie o. 5² die Witan an; s. d. Gl 3a; Frieden 1a
Here, as above 5², Eadgar addresses the Witan; see that word in Gl 3a; Frieden 1a
Die Versio schliesst homiletisch; mit Valete in Christo enden aber auch Testamente; z. B. Earle Landchar. 221
The Versio closes homiletically; but wills too end with Valete in Christo; e.g. Earle Landchar. 221
Liebermann takes this to refer to Edgar’s councillors.
